text: When you send a message on a modern messaging app, it does not travel across the internet as plain text. It is transformed by a rule into something unreadable. Only the receiver, who knows the rule, can turn it back into the original message. Now suppose you intercepted one such message, and you also knew what the original text was. Could you work out the rule? And once you had it, could you read the next message? That is exactly what a coding-decoding question asks you to do. The encryption is far simpler, of course, but the thinking process is the same.
